note: Need-now priors (EE-028): for each venture record type, the probability a venture needs it in each phase, raised or lowered by facts about the venture. Version 0.x: ours and unevaluated; Jev re-scores them per venture once the scorer runs. A record suggested at 0.5 or more in the current phase; mentioned as coming soon when the next phase reaches 0.5; otherwise held back unless the builder asks.

venture-profile.why: A few sentences on what the venture is; cheap and always useful

product.why: A product card once there is something to offer; in Discovery only if a product idea exists

account.why: Named customers, clients or members; needed once specific accounts matter

telos.why: Start with the end once past Discovery (check-telos warns from then)

validation-problem.why: The first thing to show with evidence

validation-solution.why: Once a solution is being tested

validation-pricing.why: Once someone is asked to pay

validation-go-to-market.why: Choose the path early; channels matter from Validation

validation-team.why: Skills needed versus held; first for a cofounder-first venture

validation-operations-readiness.why: Matters once others work in the venture

anatomy-answers.why: Product roles only matter with more than one product

handoff.why: Work handed to agents or people

evidence.why: Results of checks on handed-off work

decision-rights.why: Who may decide what, once anyone but the owner acts

pillar.why: Product, brand and business pillar notes as the venture grows

ownership.why: The cap table, once anyone else owns or will own a share

founder-agreement.why: Required once two or more founders share ownership. In Discovery a founding team works on it beside validation, at a lower priority than proving the problem, and a founder looking for cofounders gets the kit early (EE-060)

board.why: A formal board comes with a priced round; an advisory board is optional

exit.why: Exit paths matter once investors expect one, or the owners plan one

internal-terms.why: The venture's own internal terms (unannounced codenames, jargon) are needed before anything is published, so the leak check knows them

team-plan.why: Who the venture needs and where a human stays in the loop, once agents or others work in it

provenance.why: Written by the interfaces on every write, so it costs nothing; run mentura baseline once to adopt records written before it (EE-031)

naive-config.why: Every default holds without it; write one only to change a default: a route that fails closed, a check that only warns, a pinned package

knowledge-sources.why: Only once some records live outside the venture folder (a team repository, a CRM, a wiki); until then the folder is the whole knowledge layer

where-used.why: Once one fact (a price, a product name, a plan's limits) is repeated in several places, such as a site, newsletters and a payment provider; before launch there is rarely more than one copy

freshness-log.why: Written by mentura revalidate, verify and phase; costs nothing until a fact changes outside the venture, a record is checked without changing it, or the venture changes phase or pivots

department.why: Departments are imported one at a time; each has its own priors in operations/departments.json, listed below

icp.why: Who you serve is a foundation statement: say it early and keep it in front of you (EE-051)

goal.why: Goals are the canonical end and measures every framework writes to; state them early

exit-criteria.why: The lifecycle gate reads them: say what must be true to leave this phase

requirement.why: Requirements derive from goals once there is something to build against

constraints.why: What the venture must not do holds whatever framework it thinks in

alignment.why: How your products and agents must behave is a foundation statement; say it before you delegate to agents (EE-053)

anatomy-input.why: Only when one product has parts that need their own roles, as Naive and Mentura do; follows the anatomy answers prior

decision-impact.why: Written when a decided version is merged; worth reading once records in several functions depend on one another

decision-record.why: The decisions still owed, with what each depends on; useful once a venture has more than a handful of open questions (EE-054)

idea-dump.why: Everything the founder already thinks about the venture, before any framework asks; the cheapest way to start Discovery (EE-059)

idea-map.why: Shows where the founder's ideas cluster and what the dump never mentions, on one canvas (EE-059)

idea-graph.why: Which ideas to develop next, which must move in order and which can move on their own (EE-060)

site-presence.why: Whether the public site says what the audiences the venture courts now need to learn, once it has a site (EE-062)

marketing-sitemap.why: Which information the public site shows where, for whom and why, before engineering builds it (EE-064)

marketing-content.why: Public variants of the venture's records, gated before they are published (EE-064)

venture-package.why: What the founder walks away with; written at the end of each pipeline run, cheap to refresh

release.why: A release to hand someone (an investor, a partner, a hire): the confirmed records frozen in, with named live holes (C-11, I-17). Built with node schema/build-release.mjs when someone outside needs it

customer.why: Master data once a named customer exists. Never a completion gate (EE-070).

investor.why: Master data once a named investor exists. Never a completion gate (EE-070).

money-account.why: Master data once a named account of money exists. Never a completion gate (EE-070).

data-stream.why: An activity stream beside a master record. Held until that record exists (EE-070).

raw-source.why: A founder-supplied source. Held until the founder brings one in (EE-070).

raw-text.why: The text of a raw source, beside source.json (EE-070).

judgment.why: Never written by hand: a judgment is what a package's model step answers when mentura steps run asks it, so there is nothing to suggest

people.why: Who is in the venture and which functions each owns; create-venture writes it

founder.why: One file per founder, written by create-venture; links to the founder agreement

fund-thesis.why: A fund's foundation: what it invests in and why it wins

fund-terms.why: What the fund raises under; LPs ask for it first

deal.why: A fund's pipeline, once it is investing

money-summary.why: Written by the money source's sync; cash and runway once money moves

marketing-brand.why: One brand every agent and interface reads (colors, licensed typefaces, voice rules, marks), once the venture shows itself in public

marketing-design-system.why: One brand every agent and interface reads (colors, licensed typefaces, voice rules, marks), once the venture shows itself in public

public-assets.why: The source, license and credit of every file the venture ships as it is, before anything with rights attached is published

glossary.why: A package's own terms, once two packages start using one word in different senses

artifact.why: A view built from records for a reader; needed once something goes out to people, which grows with each phase

activity.why: Derived from transcripts by naive activity --write; worth having once the founder wants to see time spent and the streak, never required

activity-summary.why: Days since last touch and the streak feed the docket; derived, never required

publications.why: What is live and who approved it; needed from the first publication on

validation-interview.why: Problem interviews are the evidence Discovery and Validation stand on; they fade once retention holds

validation-feedback.why: Testers' checkpoint feedback, once someone is using what was built

bug.why: Bugs matter once people use the product; stable means no open P0 or P1

telemetry-event.why: Opt-in usage events; only for ventures in the plugin beta or on Mentura, and only when someone turns them on
